claim_verdicts.evidence: OrdersController.cs:21 `var customerId = int.Parse(User.FindFirstValue(JwtRegisteredClaimNames.Sub)!);` :22-24 maps request.Items to `new OrderItem {...}` .ToList(); :26 `await orderService.PlaceOrderAsync(customerId, items)`; :27 `return CreatedAtAction(nameof(Get), new { id = order.Id }, ToDto(order));`. Reading `sub` literally works because Program.cs sets `options.MapInboundClaims = false`.

"A 201 status code is generated by the CreatedAtAction method when a product is created. ... A `Location` response header containing the newly created product's URL is provided." (>= aspnetcore-8.0). Round 2: section 7 now says the Location points at the new order's URL via `Get`; OrdersController.cs:30-31 `[HttpGet("{id:int}")] ... Get(int id)` sits right after Create, and Create passes `new { id = order.Id }`, so the URL is /api/v1/orders/{id}.

Create (lines 19-28) has no `if` and no SaveChangesAsync. OrderService.cs: `if (items.Count == 0) throw new ArgumentException("an order needs at least one item");`. ExceptionHandlingMiddleware: `catch (ArgumentException ex) { ... Status400BadRequest ... }`, registered first in Program.cs:67. Round 2 suggested answer now conditions the 400 on throwing ArgumentException, which matches (other types fall to the 500 catch).

OrdersController.cs:58-63 `private static OrderDto ToDto(Order order) => new(order.Id, order.CustomerId, order.Status, order.PlacedAt, order.Items.Select(i => new OrderItemDto(i.ProductId, i.Quantity, i.UnitPriceVnd)).ToList());` Round 3 lead-in 'with `OrderItemDto` as the shape of each item' holds: Dtos.cs:9 `record OrderDto(..., List<OrderItemDto> Items)`, Dtos.cs:7 `record OrderItemDto(int ProductId, int Quantity, int UnitPriceVnd)`.

`public sealed class ProductsController(DonHangDbContext db) : ControllerBase`; List uses `db.Products.Select(...).ToListAsync()`, Get uses `db.Products.FindAsync(id)`. No service or repository involved.

OrderServiceTests: `var service = new OrderService(repository, notifier); var order = await service.PlaceOrderAsync(customerId: 1, items: [OneItem]);` with `new FakeOrderRepository()` / `new FakeNotifier()`; `PlaceOrderAsync_NoItems_Throws` asserts ArgumentException. No HTTP types referenced.

Design principle the lesson exists to teach (outline items 1-2, verbatim in spirit); the lesson itself states the exception (ProductsController), so it is not presented as a universal fact about the codebase. No version-dependent behaviour.

Checkable against the repo: OrderServiceTests constructs OrderService directly and calls PlaceOrderAsync; no code path from those tests reaches OrdersController.Create, so any check placed only in Create is not executed for them.

change-tracking/index.md:11 "These tracked entities in turn drive the changes to the database when SaveChanges is called." saving/basic.md:17 "The data will be inserted into the database when you call DbContext.SaveChanges". Repo: OrderService.cs:20 `await repository.SaveChangesAsync();`; EfOrderRepository.cs:18 `public Task SaveChangesAsync() => db.SaveChangesAsync();`. Create (OrdersController.cs:19-28) contains neither call.

web-api/index.md:182 (moniker >= aspnetcore-7.0, covers 10.0): "[FromBody] is inferred for complex type parameters not registered in the DI Container." OrdersController has [ApiController] (line 10); CreateOrderRequest is a record (Dtos.cs:13) and Program.cs registers no CreateOrderRequest service (only OrderService, repositories, DbContext).
